note: The method library (P3 of the AI-generated Paths design, 2026-11-06): the training methods a Path the catalogue adds may build its reps from, each with the library cards behind it, where it works, where it fails and its expected size in words; and the methods no Path may use, each with the card that rules it out. The compiler refuses a new Path's rep that names no method from here, or one that is blocked.

methods.name: The real thing, with a goal
methods.what: A real interaction or performance, with one specific goal written first, rather than practice that stays in the head or the room.
methods.works: Practising a social skill changed behaviour where watching others did not, and its effect on behaviour held where knowledge faded.
methods.fails: Rehearsed skills were not used in the real situation in one study, and training effects shrink the further a measure stands from the training room.

methods.name: Say what you expect, then compare
methods.what: One line before the rep on what you expect, and one tap after on how it went against that.
methods.works: People expected conversations with strangers to go worse than they did, and were liked more than they guessed; a week of short conversations made them less pessimistic, for at least a week.
methods.fails: A changed expectation faded within a week or two in experiments, so it is met again before it fades.
methods.size: Expectations moved within a week; the lasting size is not known.

methods.name: Step by step toward what you avoid
methods.what: Situations you find harder, met in a varied order and setting, staying long enough to learn what actually happens.
methods.works: Psychological treatments, mostly exposure, reduced the fear of public speaking and the gains held; for social anxiety, cognitive-behavioural therapy and exposure with skills training did better than waiting.
methods.fails: Its trials are of people with social anxiety, and the advantage of variety over one fixed order is supported only in part.
methods.size: From treatment trials; the size for everyday nerves is not known.

methods.name: One crutch dropped
methods.what: One habit used to feel safe (rehearsed lines, avoiding eyes, the phone in hand) left out on purpose.
methods.works: Dropping the small habits used to feel safe, and turning attention outward, made people come across better and feel better, in experiments on social anxiety.
methods.fails: Tested in social anxiety; the size for everyday nerves is uncertain.

methods.name: An if-then plan to start
methods.what: When a stated moment comes, the rep begins: a plan for starting and for an obstacle, never a script for the rep itself.
methods.works: If-then plans made people act on their goals more often, most for those who plan poorly.
methods.fails: Small for recurring effortful behaviour, and a rigid plan can cost flexibility.
methods.size: Small on average once publication bias is allowed for.

methods.name: Keeping your own record
methods.what: Each rep and what you did in it, kept where you can see it, beside a specific goal.
methods.works: Monitoring progress and specific goals each raised goal attainment, more when the record was kept and seen.
methods.fails: From health behaviour, not from learning a skill with others; monitoring alone moves little.

methods.name: Spread out, not crammed
methods.what: Reps spread across days and weeks rather than massed into one sitting.
methods.works: Spacing improved retention of what was learned, for knowledge and for motor skills.
methods.fails: Never tested on everyday social skills; the best gap is not known for them.

methods.name: Different people and places
methods.what: The same skill practised with different people, group sizes and settings, then tried once where it has not been practised.
methods.works: Varying the reps, people and settings is recommended to make gains last, and does no harm.
methods.fails: Its advantage over one fixed order is supported only in part.

methods.name: Practice at the edge of your ability
methods.what: Effortful practice on one specific part, a little beyond what is easy, with feedback, repeated.
methods.works: It explains part of the difference between performers.
methods.fails: It explains much less than once claimed, least in professions; hours alone promise nothing.
methods.size: About a seventh of the variance overall, far less in professions.

methods.name: Going through it in your head
methods.what: Picturing the steps of the rep before it, as preparation.
methods.works: Mental practice improved performance, though less than real practice.
methods.fails: It prepares for the rep and never replaces it.

methods.name: Checking a recording of yourself
methods.what: A recording of yourself alone, listened to the next day or later after writing what you think went wrong, then checked against a set list of behaviours.
methods.works: Video feedback against a set list of what to watch for improved trained interaction skills; how well people judge themselves tracks how well they do only weakly, and an outside view helps.
methods.fails: The studies are of professionals and medical students, with trainers; checking yourself is still your own view.
methods.size: Small to moderate in the studies of video feedback.

methods.name: Someone who was there checks the same list
methods.what: After a rep with others there, someone who was there marks which of the behaviours they noticed, on your phone.
methods.works: A teacher’s feedback improved presentation behaviour more than peers’ feedback or self-assessment; anxious speakers judged themselves more harshly than observers did.
methods.fails: One quasi-experiment in classes; the person who was there is not a trained observer.
methods.size: Not known for a check by a friend or a colleague.

methods.name: One thing done, one thing to try
methods.what: Feedback about the task, from the behaviours checked: one thing done and one thing to try next, never about you.
methods.works: Feedback helped on average, and more the more information it carried.
methods.fails: In over a third of studies it lowered performance, most when it turned attention toward the self.
methods.size: Moderate on average, and widely spread.

methods.name: A moment for the listeners
methods.what: In anything longer than a few minutes, a moment where the listeners answer or recall something.
methods.works: Recall moments between lecture segments reduced mind wandering and helped learning; a fixed attention limit lacks support.
methods.fails: From recorded lectures, not live talks.

methods.name: One point, one example, a clean ending
methods.what: A point said first, one example, and a clean ending, before any work on delivery.
methods.works: Listeners learned no more from a fluent delivery than from a halting one, which points what they keep toward content and structure.
methods.fails: No study tests a structure for a short spoken point: the shape is design judgment.

methods.name: A story that makes a point
methods.what: A short story with a turn and an ending, told because it makes one point.
methods.works: Stories changed beliefs and intentions a little, and familiar stories went over better than novel ones.
methods.fails: Studies of persuasion and of listening, not of training people to tell stories.

methods.name: A check again later
methods.what: A stage shown is checked again about a month and three months later, then about every six months.
methods.works: Unpractised skills lost about half their gain within months, and brief monthly practice kept a skill.
methods.fails: From procedural skills; the interval for conversation and speaking is not known.

methods.name: Two of your own cases side by side
methods.what: Two of your own talks or conversations compared, for what carried over and what did not.
methods.works: Comparing two cases helped people learn the principle they share and use it in new problems.

blocked.name: Power posing
blocked.why: Its effects on hormones and behaviour did not replicate.

blocked.name: Positive self-statements
blocked.why: Repeating them left people with low self-esteem feeling worse.

blocked.name: Pacing by willpower running out
blocked.why: Ego depletion did not replicate in multi-lab trials.

blocked.name: Matching to a learning style
blocked.why: The evidence needed to support it is virtually absent.

blocked.name: The SMART-goal template
blocked.why: It is not based on theory, nor consistent with the evidence on goals.
